threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You order a flat white but don’t specify oat milk, and the barista gives you that 'just-walked-in' look.
Heard a guy on the N47 bragging about winning a kebab-eating contest. By the time we got to Oval, he was asleep on his mate's shoulder, half a wrap still in hand.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a grandma arguing with a street musician over his song choice while sipping her beer outside Lidl. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not unusual to see a guy serving currywurst on a yoga mat. Only in Berlin would street food have a zen twist.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they’ve got a go-to taco spot that’s not in any guidebook, and can tell you the best time to avoid the line.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a man dramatically reenacting a Muni delay, complete with hand gestures, at the Civic Center stop. Entire crowd was oddly captivated.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all quiet squares and quaint cafés, but the reality is a nightly symphony of local kids playing fútbol in the streets until midnight.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they’re still figuring out the difference between 'café con leche' and 'café amb llet'—and asking for it everywhere.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the buses run on time – you’ll learn quickly they’re more of a suggestion than a schedule.
Heard some bloke on the 133 bragging about dodging fares for years, then the driver just laughed like it was a regular thing. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler riding a kick scooter while their dad held a beer, I thought, 'Yep, this is home.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you’re in Kreuzberg when you see a kebab shop doubling as an art gallery after 9 PM on Fridays. Only in Berlin, trust me.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively know not to stand on the left side of the BART escalator during rush hour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 today at 16th and Mission. A lady offered her spare sandwich to a guy asleep at the back. He woke up, smiled, and said, 'Best wake-up call ever.'

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about bars and squares, but they miss the tiny art studios tucked behind the main streets, full of local talent.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their bewilderment at the two-hour lunch break. They still look at their watches like it’s a 9 to 5 gig.
